title: Dispatch LTP 9: Chronicle Returns With No Edition from Tomorrow
summary: The paper resumes from a borrowed press after a day without a future issue.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: The Alderwick Chronicle returns today, printed at the Harbor Gazette’s works while its own pressroom is inspected. No issue dated tomorrow has arrived there or at the closed Chronicle office. Dr. Saye reports that the separated pieces of the old forme show no new impressions.

Mr. Ashcombe’s closure order remains in force for the original pressroom. The Chronicle did cease publication there, as the advance notice said. It missed two days of ordinary circulation. The editor has kept the notice in the archive beside the pages whose changing headlines led him to sign it.

Inspector Voss found no hidden delivery route for the future issues. The last bundle was retrieved from forty-seven doorsteps; the others have been given to the Institute or kept by their recipients. Readers who still hold them have been asked not to sell descriptions of their contents as predictions. Their ink may continue to change if a corresponding event has not passed.

Miss Marsh says the cause of the phenomenon is not settled. The forme may have drawn its words from what readers expected; the readers may have acted because of words it supplied. Both could have occurred at once. Dr. Saye has proposed a study of the saved pages, with names of private citizens concealed.

This edition contains the ordinary weather report, council notices, and the account you are reading. The compositor who set its final line was asked whether he expected a copy to arrive yesterday. “I expected to set it myself,” he said. He did.
